title: How to conduct a review | Elsevier

extracted.subtask_description: Structured, section-by-section evaluation of an original research article requiring reviewers to indicate whether comments are opinion or reflected by the data/evidence, and to check conclusions against study design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark whether comments are opinion or evidence-grounded
rubrics_metrics.description: 'You should indicate whether your comments are your own opinion or are reflected by the data and evidence.' An explicit meta-instruction: reviewers must mark which of their criticisms are evidence-grounded claim-mismatches versus personal/stylistic preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract accurately reflects all essential results and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Assess whether the abstract accurately reflects all essential aspects of the study, including all major results and limitations.' A direct instruction to check that the headline claims in the abstract are actually borne out in (and not overstated relative to) the body of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation and conclusions supported by data and study design
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The interpretation of the results and study conclusions should be supported by the data and study design.' The core claim-matching checkpoint in the Discussion section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations must be clearly emphasized as a checked criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should 'assess whether the authors have clearly emphasized the limitations of their study, including the theory, methods, and argument' - appropriate hedging/scope-limiting is itself a checked criterion, not merely a courtesy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-analyses/statistical measures needed to support what is claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether additional sub-analyses or statistical measures (CIs, effect sizes, sensitivity analyses) are needed to support what is being claimed, when reviewing the Results section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical/major data flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical/major flaws in research data are defined as: 'insufficient data points, statistically non-significant variations and unclear data tables.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Review-article reference list must cover most relevant/recent advances
rubrics_metrics.description: For review articles, reviewers should evaluate whether the reference list adequately covers 'the most relevant and recent advances in the field, including coverage of all or most relevant research groups.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether conclusions are supported by the data (best-practice DO list)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Consider feedback on the presentation of data in the article, the sustainability and reproducibility of any methodology, the analysis of any data, and whether the conclusions are supported by the data.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DON'T: 'Dismiss alternative viewpoints or theories that might conflict with your own opinions on a topic; when reviewing, maintain an open perspective' - a direct guard against a reviewer's own priors substituting for an evidence-based claim check.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI tools barred from performing the substantive evidence-claim assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The critical thinking and assessment required for peer-review are outside the scope of generative AI and AI-assisted technologies, and there is a risk that the technology will generate incorrect, incomplete or biased conclusions.' AI may be used only in a supportive capacity (e.g., improving report language, background literature search) with disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never to perform the substantive evidence-claim assessment itself, per policy.
